reforms.description: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established to provide funding for updating research infrastructure and equipment in collaboration with provinces and the private sector, as well as to support universities, colleges, hospitals, and other not-for-profit institutions in obtaining necessary research infrastructure. Measures to boost the Foundation were included in the October 2000 Budget Update.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in research infrastructure enhances the capacity for innovation and research output, which supports economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canada Foundation for Innovation was established and has been operational since 1997.
reforms.importance_rationale: The establishment of the Canada Foundation for Innovation represents a significant structural change in funding research infrastructure.
reforms.source_quote: Canada Foundation for Innovation C$1.0billion1996-97 to2002-03 Established1997 Independent not-for-profit corporation created under the Budget Implementation Act1997 to provide funding to universities, colleges, hospitals and other not-for-profit institutions to obtain necessary research infrastructure.

reforms.description: The Canada Research Chairs program was initiated to attract top researchers to Canadian universities, thereby enhancing the research landscape.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting top researchers enhances the quality of research and innovation, contributing to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The program has been operational and is contributing to the research landscape.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, the program is not as transformative as the establishment of the Canada Foundation for Innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Other recent initiatives include Canada Research Chairs to attract the best researchers to Canadian universities.

reforms.description: PRECARN was established as an industry-led consortium to assist companies in conducting research in artificial intelligence, fostering collaboration between industry and research institutions.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supporting research in artificial intelligence can lead to innovations that enhance productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The consortium has been established and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: While it supports a specific sector, it does not represent a major overhaul of the R&D landscape.
reforms.source_quote: PRECARN, an industry-led consortium to help companies undertake research in artificial intelligence.

reforms.description: The federal government launched a new Science and Technology Strategy aimed at repositioning its policies to create partnerships and networks for R&D spending, with the goal of improving Canada's R&D performance.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Creating partnerships and networks for R&D spending enhances collaboration and innovation, which can drive economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy has been launched and is in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The strategy represents a significant shift in how the government approaches R&D funding and collaboration.
reforms.source_quote: In 1994, the government had launched a wholesale policy review and repositioned its policies in a new Science and Technology Strategy.

reforms.description: The Canadian government has set an objective to double direct federal R&D spending by 2010, aiming to enhance the country's innovation capacity and competitiveness.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Doubling R&D spending is expected to significantly boost innovation capacity and economic competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The objective has been set and is being pursued.
reforms.importance_rationale: This objective represents a major commitment to enhancing R&D funding.
reforms.source_quote: Canada's official goal is to be one of the OECD’s top five R&D performers by 2010. In that perspective, the government has set an objective of doubling direct federal R&D spending by that point.

reforms.description: In March 2001, the government announced a significant investment of C$750 million for new research and development projects, building on an earlier allocation of C$500 million in the October 2000 Budget Update.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in R&D projects is expected to stimulate innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The investment was announced in March 2001.
reforms.importance_rationale: The announcement represents a significant financial commitment to R&D.
reforms.source_quote: In March 2001, the government announced that C$750 million would be spent on new research and development projects.
